beats.text: Would you have survived medieval Italy? Here are seven hundred years of murder rates.
In Italy, around fifty to seventy killings per hundred thousand people, every year.
Then, century by century, it kept falling.
Today it's below one. About sixty times lower.
Your ancestors didn't just live shorter lives. They lived far more dangerous ones.

sources: Homicide rates per 100,000 per year, Europe: Eisner (2003), 'Long-Term Historical Trends in Violent Crime', Crime and Justice 30, Table 1 (estimates per period, plotted at the period midpoint) for data up to 1985; IHME Global Burden of Disease from 1990; compiled by Our World in Data, dataset 'Homicide rates in Europe over long-term (Eisner & IHME)'. Italy: 1300 56, 1450 73, 1550 47, 1725 12, 1887 5.5, 1962 1.3, 2016 0.9 (56/0.9 = 62x). Germany & Switzerland: 1300 37 -> 2016 0.8. England: 1300 23 -> 2016 0.5.

Caveat: medieval figures are estimates from court, coroner and other records for selected regions and cities; large uncertainty. The trend (a decline by more than an order of magnitude) is consistent across regions.
